19.azegk.51: In Ashford Vale, Nils "Bones" Azegk was a shepherd. In S-C2, he is a number and a rifle. He has told everyone he intends to be a shepherd again.
The Hegemony secured Blackwater Canal. Nils "Bones" Azegk helped pass the news along the line, checking each time that he had heard correctly.

Nils "Bones" Azegk drew a line on the bench to settle an argument about space. Everyone obeyed it until the broadest man returned from duty. Nils "Bones" Azegk got a narrow grey ribbon today, the ribbon of the First Thousand. Number 871. The men who came later will ask about it.
arvidgrubb: By the time Quentin Arvidgrubb reached R-F20, the war was 3 days old and had its own habits. He learned the first one within the hour: keep your head down.
During a lull at Hill 304, Quentin Arvidgrubb called across from the Concord line. Severin Heheheha answered from the Hegemony side with a perfect imitation of an officer. Both trenches went quiet.

Quentin Arvidgrubb and Gustav Scottjseale sat through a quiet hour without finding anything to say. At the change of watch, the next pair was told it had been a good hour. The Hegemony won Hill 304. In R-F20, Quentin Arvidgrubb listened to three explanations and trusted none of them.
Quentin Arvidgrubb got a letter from Marguerite. Two pages, one of them only about the weather back home. He read that page most.
Quentin Arvidgrubb tried to describe the smell of Kesselby and got as far as the bakery. Then the ration cart arrived.
Quentin Arvidgrubb wrote back to Marguerite and tore it up three times. The fourth version says almost nothing, which is how he knows it is the right one.

Quentin Arvidgrubb was carrying water up to R-F20 when a bullet hit him in the leg. The water reached the trench. Quentin Arvidgrubb did not. Shot by Marek Dream of the Hegemony (@initial_dream8.6). A single shot at R-F20. Quentin Arvidgrubb sat down against the trench wall as if to rest, and did not get up. Shot by Marek Dream of the Hegemony (@initial_dream8.6).
The papers say Bastian Arvidgrubb. The sergeant says he has his brother's eyes. Quentin Arvidgrubb's eyes. Nobody in R-F20 argues.
From Blackwater Canal the Hegemony guns have a clear view. Bastian Arvidgrubb wrote to a younger sister who sends drawings that night and said only: 'We will take it back.'

A bullet went into Bastian Arvidgrubb's chest just under the heart at R-F20. The medic said not to give him water, and then said nothing more. Shot by Edmund "Saint" Nazareth of the Hegemony (@nazareth_2bc). Bastian Arvidgrubb was killed outright at R-F20, a single bullet from across the wire. Shot by Edmund "Saint" Nazareth of the Hegemony (@nazareth_2bc).

Edmund Arvidgrubb asked about Bastian Arvidgrubb on arriving at R-F20. The first story concerned a stolen breakfast. He asked for another. A thousand names now stand in the regimental book. Edmund Arvidgrubb is number 300. The sergeant pinned the ribbon of the First Thousand on without a speech.
bbbbbbbbennnn_kocibaaaaaaaa: Nobody saw Otto "Rabbit" Kocibaaaaaaa arrive. One morning there was simply one more helmet in U-F12, and a quiet stretcher bearer under it.
Otto "Rabbit" Kocibaaaaaaa has learned to recognize the ration cart by its squeaky wheel. This afternoon, a different squeak caused real disappointment.
breadwards.7: Jonas Breadwards reached Q-F5 expecting a speech. The welcome consisted of a mug, a space on a bench and directions to the latrine.
Jonas Breadwards took stock of his pockets: string, crumbs, a pencil and no sign of the button he was looking for.
cbour57_: Day 7. The corporal put Konrad Cbour beside a veteran and said to copy everything except the language.
A shell landed close to R-S4. When the dust settled Konrad Cbour was still there, holding a rosary of rough beads, laughing without sound.
A rat stole Konrad Cbour's cheese ration while he watched. He let it. The rat looked hungrier.

The Concord sentry, Wendel Sharky, shouted once. Konrad Cbour silenced the shout with the flat of a shovel and was back over the parapet a minute later. (@just_sharky24) Konrad Cbour went over with the night raiders and never came back. The flare caught Konrad Cbour on the wire, halfway home.
The House of Cbour sent another. Clement "Spark" Cbour, cousin of Konrad Cbour, arrived with the same eyes and the same stubborn silence.

Clement "Spark" Cbour pressed his ear to the tunnel wall under Verdel Ridge and heard it: tapping. Someone is digging toward him. The clerk counted the names twice. Clement "Spark" Cbour is number 477 of the first thousand to answer the call, and wears the ribbon of the First Thousand.
cool.dude._64: Benedikt Dude arrived with the Day 9 draft, carrying a dented harmonica and the news from home, which was old by the time he told it.
The Hegemony hold Blackwater Canal now, and they can see straight into T-F6. Benedikt Dude has learned to walk bent double.
Benedikt Dude checked the safety catch three times before handing over the post. The man taking over noticed, and checked it once more.
harry_white_y: At the depot, Felix "Button" White had practised answering to his name. At S-R18, the first person to call it only wanted help with a crate.

Felix "Button" White crawled through a gap in the Hegemony wire and slid into their trench. Albin Weyer reached for a rifle. Felix "Button" White was faster with the sharpened shovel. (@wout.vd.weyer) From Blackwater Canal the Hegemony guns have a clear view. Felix "Button" White wrote to his mother, who writes every Sunday that night and said only: 'We will take it back.'

Felix "Button" White found an old shopping list inside a coat pocket. Soap, lamp oil, apples. He folded it along the original creases. Mail came up the line with a letter for Felix "Button" White. Felix "Button" White read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.
heathcliff_grothe: Cyril Grothe, a dance-hall violinist from Wyvern Cross, was sent forward on Day 9 to fill a gap in S-C6. The gap had a name once. Nobody says it.
Victory at Blackwater Canal. Cyril Grothe let himself talk about leave for the first time in days.

Frost made each footprint distinct. Cyril Grothe followed a trail to the missing ration sack and found the quartermaster sitting on it. The company read out the roll of the First Thousand at the dawn watch. Cyril Grothe answered to number 718.
max_latsch: Cyril "Tin" Latsch arrived on Day 4 as a replacement. The men in R-F3 had been fighting for 3 days already and looked at his clean boots like a rumour from another world.
A lice inspection interrupted a heated argument about politics. Cyril "Tin" Latsch pointed out that at least one enemy had been positively identified.

Out on the wire with the wiring party. A bullet went through Cyril "Tin" Latsch's sleeve at R-F3 and took some skin with it. He kept the sleeve. Word came down the line: Hill 304 is ours. Cyril "Tin" Latsch shook hands with a corporal he had never spoken to. Today, everyone was a friend.
Cyril "Tin" Latsch wore a fresh bandage at R-F3 and was told to rest. He rested for about an hour.

The medics cleaned Cyril "Tin" Latsch's wound one last time and pronounced him fit. He is back to full duty at R-F3. Mail came up the line with a letter for Cyril "Tin" Latsch. Cyril "Tin" Latsch read it in the dugout and kept the envelope. Orders assigned Cyril "Tin" Latsch to work as a sapper. The first lesson began with what not to touch.
Cyril "Tin" Latsch and Ulrich Unstoppable have a secret signal: two taps on the helmet means 'still here'. They use it every night after the flares go out.

A bullet went into Cyril "Tin" Latsch's chest just under the heart at R-F3. The medic said not to give him water, and then said nothing more. Shot by Rafael Davidsonmars of the Concord (@davidsonmarshall). Cyril "Tin" Latsch was killed at R-F3 just after dawn. The cup of tea beside him was still hot. Shot by Rafael Davidsonmars of the Concord (@davidsonmarshall).

Severin Latsch asked about Cyril "Tin" Latsch on arriving at R-F3. The first story concerned a stolen breakfast. He asked for another. Now serving as a sapper, Severin Latsch discovered that being experienced at the front did not prevent being new at the job.

Blackwater Canal fell to the Hegemony at dusk. Severin Latsch helped drag the guns up the slope and slept that night on ground nobody else had held for years. Mail came up the line with a letter for Severin Latsch. Severin Latsch read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.

The patrol came back one man at a time. Severin Latsch held the gap open and counted until the corporal said that was everyone. Mail came up the line with a letter for Severin Latsch. Severin Latsch read it in the dugout and kept the envelope. The company read out the roll of the First Thousand at the dawn watch. Severin Latsch answered to number 270.
schildbroete: The sergeant gave Rafael Schildbroete a dead man's blanket and a living man's job. That is how replacements start, on Day 6 or any other. Rafael Schildbroete became a machine gunner today. He wrote the change in a letter home, then crossed out the explanation and tried again.
Ivo Warrior and Rafael Schildbroete divided a parcel using a tin lid as scales. The last crumb needed a second opinion.
Rafael Schildbroete fixed the strap on Ivo Warrior's pack. The price was a biscuit and a promise to stop mentioning the haircut.
Rafael Schildbroete of the Concord and Viktor Ssprinklez of the Hegemony watched a broken branch near the Sunken Road all morning. Neither could risk assuming it was only a branch.
A letter reached Rafael Schildbroete from Millbank. The streets there still have names. He read them out loud, one by one.
Day 10: Blackwater Canal was lost. Rafael Schildbroete wrote down the news without trying to explain it.

A periscope poked up from the enemy line. Rafael Schildbroete shot it to pieces, and the man holding it, Yann "Saint" Ain, was grazed. The company read out the roll of the First Thousand at the dawn watch. Rafael Schildbroete answered to number 402.
the_skyler_of_chandlerz: On the way to P-F2, Anselm Chandlerz tried to memorise every turn. By the dugout door, he was simply glad someone else knew the way.

Anselm Chandlerz caught himself counting portions before counting people. He started again. A letter from home reached Anselm Chandlerz before dusk. Anselm Chandlerz read it twice and slept a little easier.
